Contribution margin vs ROAS

A 3x ROAS can still lose money.

ROAS counts revenue, not what that revenue cost to deliver. Product, shipping, fees and returns come out first. Switch the ROAS below and watch the same order flip from loss to profit.

Attribution

One order. Three dashboards claim it.

A customer sees a Reel, searches your brand and buys. Each platform counts the sale under its own rules, so the dashboards add up to more revenue than you banked.

How we handle it

We judge the account on the total: revenue in your store and bank against total ad spend. Platform numbers are used to compare campaigns inside one platform, not to add up the business.

Payback

The first order loses. The repeat pays.

A ₹400 customer who buys once for ₹1,000 is a 2.5x ROAS: below break-even, so most dashboards call it a failure. If that customer comes back, the same ad spend turns into profit.

So for brands with repeat buyers we judge acquisition on how fast a customer pays back, not on the first order alone.

Orders per customer

Assumes ₹400 to acquire a customer, ₹300 contribution per order (30% of ₹1,000), and no extra ad spend on repeat orders. Illustration, not a client result. Your repeat rate sets your real payback.

Creative, content and UGC

Creative decides who stops scrolling.

On Meta, YouTube and quick commerce, the ad itself does most of the targeting and most of the selling. So we run creative as a testing programme, not a one-off shoot, and judge every new angle on the same contribution margin as the media.

  1. 01

    Brief

    One brand thesis, then several angles: the hook, the offer and the proof, written before anything is shot.

  2. 02

    Shoot

    Creator and UGC-style video, founder and product footage, shot so it can be cut into many ads.

  3. 03

    Edit

    Hooks, lengths and formats cut from the same footage, plus statics and carousels.

  4. 04

    Test

    Angles run against each other on a fixed budget, with a rule agreed up front for what counts as a winner.

  5. 05

    Refresh

    Creative tires. New versions of the winners go in before results slip.

Common questions

What people ask first.

What does MMC's performance marketing cover?

Media buying on Meta, Google, Amazon and quick commerce, plus the creative and reporting that go with it, run as one account structure for D2C brands.

Meta, Google, Amazon or quick commerce: what comes first?

Start where your buyers already look for you and where your margin can carry the spend. We settle the order in the audit, against your break-even ROAS.

How is success measured?

On contribution margin, and on blended results reconciled to your store data, not on platform-reported ROAS. Break-even ROAS is the floor. It is revenue per order divided by contribution per order, and you can work yours out with the free break-even ROAS calculator.

What does it cost?

It depends on ad spend and scope, so we quote after the audit call, once we have seen your accounts.

Do you work with B2B and education brands?

Yes. This page is about D2C, but we also run lead generation for B2B companies and educational institutes. There the goal is qualified leads and enrolments, not baskets and repeat orders, so the work is set up differently. See the B2B and education pages.

Is there a minimum commitment?

We agree terms on the audit call, once we know what you need.

What is break-even ROAS?

Revenue per order divided by contribution per order. Below it, you are paying for revenue instead of profit. Try the break-even ROAS calculator.
